`git fetch` downloads new commits and updates remote-tracking branches (like `origin/main`), but leaves your current branch and working files unchanged.

`git pull` runs a fetch, then integrates the changes into your current branch—usually by merging or rebasing, depending on your configuration. This can cause conflicts.
